gen-silkscreen-gf-electrolize: Silkscreen spaces its blocky pixel letters so far apart you can nearly feel the gaps between them. Electrolize handles the reading with a modern, open-jawed c, doing the quiet work while the heading plays the retro showpiece.
gen-silkscreen-gf-elms-sans: Silkscreen leaves lots of breathing room around each pixel letter. Elms Sans follows in a plain sans line with the pressure-free feel of a ballpoint, so the lo-fi heading and the modern body sit together without any fuss.
gen-silkscreen-gf-encode-sans: Encode Sans keeps its letters distinct, with gaps that stop c from collapsing into o. Silkscreen above it holds a steady weight from word to word, which gives this pair its strongest quality: retro attitude over tidy, clean text.
gen-silkscreen-gf-encode-sans-expanded: Silkscreen puts generous space around every letter, a lo-fi spaghetti line of pixel type that feels retro at once. Encode Sans Expanded is the plain sans counterpart, with tips pulled wide apart and a friendly, approachable manner for the text.
gen-silkscreen-gf-encode-sans-sc: Silkscreen draws its curves and straights at the same line width, so everything looks cut from one retro grid. Encode Sans SC brings a shallow terminal curl and a wide gap, and that crisp, professional restraint is what makes the pair so easy to trust.
gen-silkscreen-gf-encode-sans-semi-conde: Silkscreen runs a monoline stroke from start to finish, giving lo-fi pixel letters plenty of space between them while the body stays modern. Encode Sans Semi Condensed brings sans-serif openness on the s, which is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-silkscreen-gf-encode-sans-semi-expan: Retro to its core, Silkscreen skims along on a stroke weight that never changes, with space around every letter. And Encode Sans Semi Expanded gives it a contemporary sans-serif partner whose rounded letters stay open, which is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-silkscreen-gf-exo: Exo carries the text with wide gaps that keep even tiny sizes crisp, and its approachable sans-serif shapes stay clear. Silkscreen overhead draws bowls and stems at the same weight, so the strongest quality is a retro heading that never crowds.
gen-silkscreen-gf-exo-2: Silkscreen is lo-fi and retro, with diagonals matching its stems. Exo 2 does the opposite job, offering a plain sans body with curves that leave plenty of daylight inside, clean and professional where the heading is playful.
gen-silkscreen-gf-faculty-glyphic: Retro and lo-fi, Silkscreen gives its tails and terminals the same thickness as its main stems, with space around every letter. And Faculty Glyphic follows with a modern sans body whose rounded letters stay clearly open, so reading feels unhurried.
